title: Critical! catalogue, format 9
description: Shape of the catalogue artifact (ADR 0021): the spells and the PHB rule tables (step 9), the class and race tables (step 10, ADR 0030 step 23), the racial level limits (step 11, DMG Table 7), each priest spell's sphere codes and the classes' sphere access (step 12, ADR 0030 steps 15 and 23), the equipment reference data and its two rule tables (step 13, ADR 0033 steps 21 to 23), the language catalogue and each race's language list (step 14, ADR 0032 step 4) and the non-weapon proficiency descriptions (step 16, ADR 0037 step 19). The API reads format 9 only: formats 3 to 8 were each the same shape without the parts added later, and are retired (step 16.5). Shape only: the schema carries no book text.

format.description: Artifact format: 9 (ADR 0021 step 16: the formats 3 to 8 plus the non-weapon proficiency descriptions). An importer accepts exactly the formats it knows and refuses the rest.

version.description: Content version, UTC build date YYYY-MM-DD with an optional .N suffix for several builds on a day. Compared for equality only, never ordered.

localized.description: English is required; French is optional and the app falls back to English when it is absent. An absent language is omitted, never an empty string.

description.description: Text in the Markdown subset of ADR 0021 step 1: blocks separated by exactly one blank line; a block is a paragraph (one line, no hard wrap), a bullet list (lines starting with "- ") or a pipe table (lines starting and ending with "|"); no headings, no HTML, no leading or trailing whitespace. The pattern checks the block structure; the builder also checks table delimiter rows.

id.description: Stable key, never changes once published (spellbook, spell effects, slots and undo history reference it). The builder keeps it in a published-id ledger (ADR 0021 step 3).

school.description: Raw school text as the book prints it; may hold several, e.g. "Alteration, Evocation".

sphere.description: Priest spells only (raw text, may hold several spheres). Omitted for Wizard spells.

spheres.description: Format 6, priest spells only: the spell's spheres as language-neutral codes (e.g. all, combat, elemental_fire, thought), one per sphere of the raw sphere text, Elemental as its subsphere codes (ADR 0030 step 23). The engine reads these, never the raw text.

source.description: Provenance of the English text, 2 to 8 upper-case characters: a book code (PHB, TOM) or WEB for text of the original web scrape that no book has been matched to.

rule_tables.description: The rule tables the engine looks values up in (ADR 0021 steps 9 and 10): numbers and language-neutral codes only, the columns the engine reads, rows in ascending order. Format 3 carries the first four tables only, format 4 every table but race_level_limits, format 5 every table but sphere_access, format 6 every table but weapon_vs_armor and initiative_item, format 7 every table. Contiguity, overlap, level order, increasing XP and completeness of the code combinations cannot be expressed here: the builder and the importer check them.

sphere_access.description: Format 6: the spheres each class has access to (ADR 0030 step 15.1), one row per class and sphere; a sphere a class has no row for is closed to it. Minor access opens spell levels 1 to 3 only (an engine rule).

weapon_vs_armor.description: Format 7: PHB Table 52 (optional rule), the modifier of each armour type (a row code of the equipment) against each damage type (s slashing, p piercing, b bludgeoning); exactly one row per armour row (ADR 0033 steps 19 and 21). The engine reads the damage type of the attack against the target's armour row.

race_languages.description: Format 8: each race's language list (PHB chapter 2, the Languages paragraph of each race, ADR 0032 step 4): one row per race and language of its list, native marking the race's own language (exactly one per race; Common for a human and a half-elf). The language is a code of the artifact's languages.

initiative_item.description: Format 7: PHB Table 56 (optional rule), the initiative modifier of a magic item by its magic kind (ADR 0033 steps 15 and 21); one row per kind. A scroll has no modifier: the spell's casting time counts, so its row carries none.

strength_row.description: PHB Table 1: a range of Strength scores, and for 18 a range of the 18/xx percentile.

exc_min.description: 18/xx percentile, 100 = 18/00; 0 with exc_max 0 = no exceptional part.

dexterity_row.description: PHB Table 2: a range of Dexterity scores.

defensive.description: Defensive adjustment to AC (negative improves it).

bard_spells_row.description: PHB Table 32: the spells a bard of that level casts per day.

per_spell_level.description: Spells per day of spell levels 1 to 6.

bard_experience_row.description: PHB Table 25, Thief/Bard column: the XP that reaches the level.

experience_row.description: PHB Tables 14 (Fighter), 20 (Mage), 23 (Cleric), 25 (Thief/Bard): the XP that reaches the level, per class.

hit_dice_row.description: PHB Tables 14, 20, 23, 25 (Hit Dice column): the group's hit die, the last level that rolls it, and the fixed hit points gained per level after it.

constitution_row.description: PHB Table 3: hit point adjustment per die (every class, and the warriors' own), and the value a low die counts as (0 = none).

intelligence_row.description: PHB Table 4: highest spell level (0 = none), chance to learn a spell in percent, maximum spells per level (absent = no maximum).

wisdom_row.description: PHB Table 5: the bonus spells this score adds (spell levels, not cumulative) and the chance of spell failure in percent.

con_save_bonus_row.description: PHB Table 9: saving throw bonus by Constitution.

race_requirement_row.description: PHB Table 7: the score range a race allows for an ability (before the racial adjustments).

race_adjustment_row.description: PHB Table 8: a race's ability adjustment (abilities not listed: 0).

race_level_limit_row.description: DMG Table 7: the highest level a race reaches in a class: max_level 1 to 20, 0 = the race cannot belong to the class (the book's dash), absent = no racial limit (the book's U). Humans have no row (no limit in any class).

thac0_row.description: PHB Table 53: THAC0 per group at the level.

saving_throw_row.description: PHB Table 60: the five save targets of a group over a level band (levels 1 to 20).

level_rate_row.description: PHB Table 15: warrior melee attacks per round over a level band, as attacks per rounds.

specialist_attack_row.description: PHB Table 35: a specialist's attacks per round with a weapon over a level band.

rate_of_fire_row.description: PHB Table 45 (ROF): a missile weapon type's rate of fire, as attacks per rounds.

wizard_spells_row.description: PHB Table 21: the spells a wizard of that level memorizes, spell levels 1 to 9.

priest_spells_row.description: PHB Table 24: the spells a priest of that level prays for, spell levels 1 to 7.

priest_spell_wisdom_row.description: PHB Table 24's notes: the Wisdom a priest needs to use spells of that level.

skill_base_row.description: PHB Table 26 (thief) or 33 (bard): a skill's base score in percent.

skill_race_row.description: PHB Table 27: a race's adjustment to a thieving skill, in percentage points.

skill_dexterity_row.description: PHB Table 28: Dexterity adjustments to the five skills it changes, in percentage points (scores outside the rows: 0).

skill_armor_row.description: PHB Table 29: an armour's adjustment to a thieving skill, in percentage points (leather is the baseline, 0).

bard_armor_penalty_row.description: PHB Table 29's note: the bard's extra adjustment in non-elven (metal) chain mail, added to the elven chain column.

backstab_row.description: PHB Table 30: backstab damage multiplier over a level band.

turning_row.description: PHB Table 61: an undead type (and its Hit Dice: hd_max absent = and more, both absent = by type only) and the cell for each priest level 1 to 20.

turning_cell.description: Either roll (success on a d20 at or above it) or outcome (no die: turned, destroyed, destroyed and 2d4 more, or cannot turn).

damage_expr.description: A damage as printed: dice NdM, a flat number, with an optional flat bonus (1d6+1, 1d3-1, 1).

equipment.description: Format 7: the equipment reference data (ADR 0033 steps 21 to 23, ADR 0021 step 13): the weapons, ammunition, body armour and shields a player picks from. Numbers and codes only, names as language maps; no book text. A character's piece copies a row and keeps its code, so the importer never keeps a row for a character.

languages.description: Format 8: the language catalogue (ADR 0032 step 4): the languages of the PHB racial lists plus Common, and any campaign language. Codes are language-neutral (ADR 0023); the names are language maps.

proficiency_descriptions.description: Format 9: the description of each non-weapon proficiency of ADR 0037 step 2's catalogue (ADR 0021 step 16): exactly 65 rows, one per proficiency id, in English and French, each in step 1's Markdown subset. The name stays an i18n key by id and the figures stay in seeds/proficiencies.json, so a row carries nothing else. That every catalogue id has a row is the builder's and the importer's check (the ids are data, not schema).

description.description: Both languages are required (spells require English only): a proficiency pop-up has a text in either language.

weapon_row.description: PHB Table 44 weapon row. A launcher (fires) has a speed but no damage: its ammunition's rows carry the dice. damage_sm / damage_l go together.

fires.description: A launcher's ammunition kinds (a blowgun fires two).

ammunition_row.description: An ammunition row of PHB Table 44 (arrow, quarrel, bullet, stone, needle, dart).

armour_row.description: A body armour (PHB Table 44, Table 46, with elven chain mail, DMG): base_ac is Table 46 without a shield; skill_column the Table 29 column (none_allowed: an armour a thief or bard may not wear); armor_row the Table 52 row.

shield_row.description: A shield (PHB p.75-76): its AC bonus against melee and against missiles.
